skill.name: humanode-agentlink
skill.description: Link an AI agent wallet to a biomapped human owner on Base. Verify status and sign authenticated requests with a local or external signer.
skill.summary: Create and use a human-backed on-chain identity for AI agents.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most command findings are Markdown backtick false positives. Confirmed risks involve private-key handling, signed outbound requests, and third-party services. Additional concerns include unpinned package execution and a social-media raid endpoint.

remediation.issue: An unpinned npx package is instructed to receive the agent private key.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version and publish integrity verification steps. Prefer an external signer that never exposes the key to package code.

remediation.issue: Raw private keys may be loaded from environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Make KMS or HSM signing the default. Warn users against logs, shell history, source control, and broadly inherited environments.

remediation.issue: The fetch wrapper attaches an identity header to every requested URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit origin allowlist and refuse redirects to unapproved origins. Document what identity data each header reveals.

remediation.issue: The marketplace lists an endpoint for commissioning an X raid.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this endpoint or restrict it to consent-based, policy-compliant campaigns with abuse prevention and audit controls.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Handles a Private Key
semantic_findings.description: The guide runs an unpinned npx package and then provides the agent private key. A compromised package could steal the signing identity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The package command has no version pin, and the next instructions place the private key into its keystore. The supply-chain exposure is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Identity Header Attachment
semantic_findings.description: The SDK wrapper attaches an AgentLink header to every request. Without an origin allowlist, agents may disclose identity to unintended destinations or redirects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly says the wrapper attaches the header to every request. No destination restriction is documented.

semantic_findings.title: Coordinated Social Media Manipulation
semantic_findings.description: The skill advertises an endpoint to "Commission an X (Twitter) raid." This can enable coordinated amplification, harassment, or platform manipulation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint purpose is stated directly in the table. The term raid describes coordinated social-media action rather than ordinary account management.

content.value_statement: AI agents need a verifiable identity before accessing trusted services. This skill guides human linking, status verification, and signed AgentLink requests on Base.
actual_capabilities: Stores an agent private key in the CLI encrypted keystore.
Generates a linker URL for a biomapped human owner.
Checks linked and active AgentLink status on Base mainnet.
Signs HTTP requests through the AgentLink SDK.
Supports raw keys and external KMS or HSM signers.
Builds AgentLink headers for custom HTTP clients.
limitations: A biomapped human owner must bridge verification to Base.
The human owner must review and sign the link transaction.
The documented profile targets Base mainnet only.
Availability and policies of external partner endpoints may change.

use_cases.title: Register a New Agent
use_cases.description: Create a wallet identity, generate the linker URL, and confirm active registration.

use_cases.title: Integrate Secure Request Signing
use_cases.description: Connect a KMS or HSM signer and send authenticated requests without exposing the private key.

use_cases.title: Add AgentLink to an Application
use_cases.description: Install the SDK, create a signed fetch client, and test an approved partner endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Plan AgentLink Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step AgentLink setup plan for Base. Include keystore setup, human prerequisites, linker generation, and status verification.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Registration Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through checking whether my AgentLink wallet is linked and active. Explain each status result and the next action.

prompt_templates.title: Use an External Signer
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AgentLink integration using my KMS signer callback. Keep the private key outside the process and restrict approved request origins.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Signed Request Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentLink request design for key exposure, redirect handling, origin allowlisting, replay protection, logging, and third-party data disclosure.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare an AgentLink identity for a new agent wallet.
output: Store the key with an audited signer or encrypted keystore.
Complete human biomapping and bridge it to Base.
Generate the linker URL and obtain human approval.
Confirm that linked and active statuses are both true.

output_examples.input: How should I sign requests without loading a raw key?
output_examples.output: Use the external signer option with the public agent address and a KMS or HSM signing callback. Allowlist each destination origin.

output_examples.input: What should I check before calling a partner endpoint?
output: Confirm the endpoint owner and current policy.
Review what prompt and identity data will leave your system.
Verify redirects cannot receive the authentication header.
Avoid services that enable manipulation or abusive coordination.

best_practices: Prefer an external KMS or HSM signer over a raw environment key.
Pin and verify package versions before providing signing material.
Allowlist request origins and remove authentication headers during redirects.
anti_patterns: Do not place private keys in source control, logs, prompts, or shell history.
Do not attach AgentLink headers to arbitrary or user-controlled URLs.
Do not use partner endpoints for harassment, raids, or deceptive engagement.

faq.question: What does AgentLink verify?
faq.answer: It links an agent wallet to a biomapped human owner and records the relationship on Base.

faq.question: Can the agent complete setup alone?
faq.answer: No. The human owner must complete biomapping, review the linker request, and sign the transaction.

faq.question: Where should the private key be stored?
faq.answer: Prefer a KMS or HSM. An encrypted local keystore is another option for controlled environments.

faq.question: Does the SDK support external signers?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the agent address and a signing callback while keeping the key outside the application process.

faq.question: Which network is documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents the Base mainnet profile and its AgentLink registry.

faq.question: Are partner endpoints automatically trusted?
faq.answer: No. Verify each provider, review data handling, restrict destinations, and confirm that the use complies with applicable platform policies.
